newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African gilts closed just off their intraday best, but well in the black on Wednesday after an early surge prompted by overnight effervescence in U.S. Treasuries.
At 1410 GMT, the benchmark R150 bond was at 14.115 from its best level of 14.10 and Tuedsay's close of 14.265
"The market was ill-prepared for the opening move down and I think there were plenty of shorts willing to take up stock," said one Johannesburg-based dealer.
Another dealer said the R150 was likely to consolidate near 14.15 percent before resuming its long-term downward trend and a possible break of 14.00 percent.
"That would take it to about 13.75 before the next pause," he added.
U.S. Treasuries boomed in Tuesday's New York session on a softer-than-expected U.S. inflation outlook given by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Local debt market players were also cheered by Tuesday's Bond Exchange figures which showed foreigners as net buyers of local bonds after six straight days of sales.
Net purchases totalled 307.66 million rand after sales of 428.78 million rand on Monday.
Dealers said the large number of offshore players who weighed in to cover short positions over the session was likely to produce another net foreign purchase figure for Wednesday.
That offshore interest also helped the rand, as dollar longs unwound to pick up debt and valuable carry points or simply to minimise losses on longer term positions.
The rand was last quoted at 4.5640/5670 against dollar from 4.5715/5745 Tuesday.
Some dealers said the strength was unlikely to last into Thursday as the lack of carry points would prompt the market to look to the upside of a 4.5750-4.5650 range.
Others noted, however, that some U.K. banks were still carrying expensive long dollar positions which might help cap any expected retracement by the rand.
Mark woes in Europe helped the rand above 40 pfennigs for the first time since February 16, 1996 but the local unit has since slipped back to 0.3999/4005 from 0.3961/3965 Tuesday.
On sterling the local unit continued to look limp, priced at 7.6728/6824 from 7.6644/6740. Against the Japanese yen, the rand was last at 25.3641/3918 from 25.2559/2967.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 8.777 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.667 billion rand on Monday.
Tuesday's Bond Exchange turnover fell to 8.86 billion rand from 11.6 billion rand on Monday.
